latest_release.body:
# 2.14.11 — CRA, IEC 62304 and skill hints
_Released 2026-11-11_

Two new compliance plugins: cra-readiness for the EU Cyber Resilience Act, whose Article 14 reporting already
applies, and medical-device-software for IEC 62304 and IEC 81001-5-1. Eight plugins now ship a quiet
`UserPromptSubmit` hook that names one of 21 skills that never loaded on their own when a prompt clearly fits it;
it makes no model or network calls, and `SKILL_ROUTER=0` turns it off (`SKILL_ROUTER_<PLUGIN>=0` for one plugin).
No renames, so nothing needs a reinstall: `claude plugin update` picks up the hooks, and the new plugins install
as usual. Changed plugins are bumped; plugins above 2.14.11 from earlier releases keep their versions (gate G11).

### Added

- **cra-readiness plugin: EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847)** (`ra-qm-team/cra-readiness`, also
  bundled in ra-qm-skills). Article 14 reporting has applied since 11 September 2026 to every in-scope product on
  the EU market, including products shipped before the CRA; everything else applies from 11 December 2027. Four
  deterministic stdlib scripts: `cra_scope_classifier.py` (scope and Art 2 exclusions, roles under Arts 19-22 and 24,
  Annex III/IV class, the conformity routes Art 32 allows, legacy products under Art 69, the Art 13(8) support
  period, and the CSIRT that receives reports under Art 14(7)); `art14_report_clock.py` (24 h early warning, 72 h
  notification, final report 14 days after a fix or one month after an incident notification, required content,
  user notice under Art 14(8), and the Art 64(10)(a) SME carve-out); `annex_i_gap_check.py` (39 ids across Annex I
  Parts I and II, Annex VII and Annex II, refusing NA on vulnerability handling); `sbom_check.py` (CycloneDX or SPDX
  JSON, primary component, top-level dependencies per Annex I Part II(1)). Ships the cs-cra-officer agent,
  `/cs-cra-readiness` and `/cs-cra-report`, three references citing the regulation, Implementing Regulation (EU)
  2025/2392 and Commission guidance C(2026) 5252, and an Article 14 runbook.
- **Skill hints for 21 skills that never loaded on their own.** Eight plugins (engineering-skills,
  engineering-advanced-skills, marketing-skills, product-skills, c-level-skills, agenthub, autoresearch-agent,
  si) now ship a `UserPromptSubmit` hook, `hooks/skill_router.py`, that names the fitting skill when a prompt
  clearly matches one (tdd-guide, senior-backend/frontend/devops/secops/data-scientist, gcp-cloud-architect,
  minimalist, codebase-onboarding, self-eval, tech-debt-tracker, copy-editing, content-humanizer,
  marketing-psychology, experiment-designer, product-manager-toolkit, roadmap-communicator, cto-advisor,
  agenthub, autoresearch-agent, remember). Silent otherwise, one hint per plugin per prompt, once per session,
  no model or network calls; `SKILL_ROUTER=0` turns it off. Measured live on held-out prompts: the skills
  loaded in 24/84 runs with the hook against 2/84 without, and 0/21 on near misses either way. No new commands:
  every skill is already `/<plugin>:<skill>`. Per-skill decisions in `audit/silent-skill-triggers-2026-11/`;
  `scripts/check_skill_router.py` (CI) keeps the copies identical and the routes valid.
- Daily triage pipeline for community PRs and issues: `scripts/triage_snapshot.py` lists every open item with mechanical signals (CI or manifest changes, network and LLM calls in added code, new dependencies, external domains, commercial wording, untouched issue templates) and a suggested lane, without executing or echoing contributor text. `.github/TRIAGE_POLICY.md` sets the pipeline from snapshot to draft PR on `dev`, the documentation update every PR carries, release prep (CHANGELOG version entry, version lines, the `dev → main` PR, with the tag left to `release.yml`), what runs without the maintainer and what waits for a per-batch go-ahead, and runs contributor code only in a network-less namespace, because every process in the cloud container inherits the ses

# Claude Code Skills & Plugins

**415 production-ready skills for Claude Code and 12 other coding agents, covering engineering, product, marketing, compliance, finance and the C-suite. We test whether each skill loads when you ask in plain words, and [publish the results](VERIFIED.md).**

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow?style=for-the-badge)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skills-415-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](#skills-overview)
[![Agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agents-131-blue?style=for-the-badge)](#agents)
[![Personas](https://img.shields.io/badge/Personas-7-purple?style=for-the-badge)](#personas)
[![Commands](https://img.shields.io/badge/Commands-173-orange?style=for-the-badge)](#commands)
[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/alirezarezvani/claude-skills?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alirezarezvani/claude-skills/stargazers)
[![SkillCheck Validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/SkillCheck-Validated-4c1?style=for-the-badge)](https://getskillcheck.com)

**Works with:** Claude Code · OpenAI Codex · Gemini CLI · OpenClaw · Hermes Agent[^hermes] · Mistral Vibe[^vibe] · Cursor · Aider · Windsurf · Kilo Code · OpenCode · Augment · Antigravity

## Install in one minute

**Claude Code**

```bash
/plugin marketplace add alirezarezvani/claude-skills
/plugin install engineering-skills@claude-code-skills
```

**Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and other agents** (the open-source [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installer)

```bash
npx skills add alirezarezvani/claude-skills
```

More options for each tool are under [Quick Install](#quick-install).

## Pick your role

| You are | Install | You get |
|---|---|---|
| Software engineer | `engineering-skills` | Architecture, code review, TDD, frontend, backend, DevOps, security, QA |
| Platform or AI engineer | `engineering-advanced-skills` | Agent design, RAG, MCP servers, CI/CD, observability, SLOs, evals |
| Product manager | `product-skills` | Discovery, RICE, PRDs, user stories, roadmaps, UX research |
| Delivery lead or scrum master | `pm-skills` | Sprint health, Jira and Confluence, flow metrics, forecasts |
| Marketer | `marketing-skills` | SEO, answer-engine optimization, copywriting, CRO, email, paid ads |
| Founder or executive | `c-level-skills` | CEO, CTO, CFO, CMO, CRO and other advisors, board prep, hard calls |
| Regulated industry | `ra-qm-skills` | ISO 13485, EU MDR, FDA, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, CAPA, risk files |
| Finance | `finance-skills` | DCF, budgets, SaaS metrics, month-end close |

Install with `/plugin install <name>@claude-code-skills`.

## Start with these

Each of these loaded on every plain-language test prompt. [See all verified skills](VERIFIED.md).

| Skill | What it does | Install |
|---|---|---|
| [agent-run-forensics](engineering/agent-run-forensics/) | Checks what your agent actually did against what it said it did, from the session transcript | `agent-run-forensics` |
| [human-gate](engineering/human-gate/) | Refuses to ship a plan, spec or migration until a named person has reviewed it and no blocker is open | `human-gate` |
| [skill-retro](engineering/skill-retro/) | Grades your skills from your own past sessions and proposes only the edits the evidence supports | `skill-retro` |
| [i18n-localization](engineering/i18n-localization/) | Finds missing keys, broken placeholders and wrong plural forms before a language ships | `i18n-localization` |
| [month-end-close](finance/month-end-close/) | Runs the close calendar, proves reconciliations and refuses boilerplate variance explanations | `month-end-close` |
| [cmmc-readiness](ra-qm-team/cmmc-readiness/) | Scores CMMC 2.0 Level 2 readiness, SPRS and POA&M close-out | `cmmc-readiness` |
| [cra-readiness](ra-qm-team/cra-readiness/) | EU Cyber Resilience Act: Article 14 reporting clock, product classes, Annex I and SBOM gates | `cra-readiness` |

[^hermes]: Hermes Agent is **BYO-sync tier**: the repo ships a pre-generated `.hermes/skills/claude-skills/` tree, but you run `python scripts/sync-hermes-skills.py` once locally to install into `~/.hermes/skills/`. Uses the same agentskills.io SKILL.md standard — no format conversion.
[^vibe]: Mistral Vibe is also **BYO-sync tier**: the repo ships a pre-generated `.vibe/skills/claude-skills/` tree, run `./scripts/vibe-install.sh` once locally to install into `~/.vibe/skills/`. Same agentskills.io SKILL.md standard — no format conversion. Docs: <https://docs.mistral.ai/mistral-vibe/agents-skills>.

---

## What Are Claude Code Skills & Agent Plugins?

Claude Code skills (also called agent skills or coding agent plugins) are modular instruction packages that give AI coding agents domain expertise they don't have out of the box. Each skill includes:

- **SKILL.md** — structured instructions, workflows, and decision frameworks
- **Python tools** — 824 CLI scripts (all stdlib-only, zero pip installs)
- **Reference docs** — 931 templates, checklists, and domain-specific knowledge files

**One repo, thirteen platforms.** Works natively as Claude Code plugins, Codex agent skills, Gemini CLI skills, Hermes Agent skills, Mistral Vibe skills, and converts to more tools via `scripts/convert.sh`. All 824 Python tools run anywhere Python runs.

### Skills vs Agents vs Personas

| | Skills | Agents | Personas |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | How to execute a task | What task to do | Who is thinking |
| **Scope** | Single domain | Single domain | Cross-domain |
| **Voice** | Neutral | Professional | Personality-driven |
| **Example** | "Follow these steps for SEO" | "Run a security audit" | "Think like a startup CTO" |

All three work together. See [Orchestration](#orchestration) for how to combine them.

---

Details: [INSTALLATION.md → Windows Notes](INSTALLATION.md#windows-notes).

## Multi-Tool Support (New)

**Convert the skills for 9 more AI coding tools** with a single script:

| Tool | Format | Install |
|------|--------|---------|
| **Cursor** | `.mdc` rules | `./scripts/install.sh --tool cursor --target .` |
| **Aider** | `CONVENTIONS.md` | `./scripts/install.sh --tool aider --target .` |
| **Kilo Code** | `.kilocode/rules/` | `./scripts/install.sh --tool kilocode --target .` |
| **Windsurf** | `.windsurf/skills/` | `./scripts/install.sh --tool windsurf --target .` |
| **OpenCode** | `.opencode/skills/` | `./scripts/install.sh --tool opencode --target .` |
| **Augment** | `.augment/rules/` | `./scripts/install.sh --tool augment --target .` |
| **Antigravity** | `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/` | `./scripts/install.sh --tool antigravity` |
| **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `python scripts/sync-hermes-skills.py --verbose` |
| **Mistral Vibe** | `~/.vibe/skills/` | `./scripts/vibe-install.sh` |

**How it works:**

```bash
# 1. Convert all skills to all tools (takes ~15 seconds)
./scripts/convert.sh --tool all

# 2. Install into your project (with confirmation)
./scripts/install.sh --tool cursor --target /path/to/project

# Or use --force to skip confirmation:
./scripts/install.sh --tool aider --target . --force

# 3. Verify
find .cursor/rules -name "*.mdc" | wc -l  # one file per skill
```

**Each tool gets:**
- ✅ All skills converted to native format
- ✅ Per-tool README with install/verify/update steps
- ✅ Support for scripts, references, templates where applicable
- ✅ Zero manual conversion work

Run `./scripts/convert.sh --tool all` to generate tool-specific outputs locally.

## Personas

Pre-configured agent identities with curated skill loadouts, workflows, and distinct communication styles. Personas go beyond "use these skills" — they define how an agent thinks, prioritizes, and communicates.

| Persona | Domain | Best For |
|---------|--------|----------|
| [**Startup CTO**](agents/personas/startup-cto.md) | Engineering + Strategy | Architecture decisions, tech stack selection, team building, technical due diligence |
| [**Growth Marketer**](agents/personas/growth-marketer.md) | Marketing + Growth | Content-led growth, launch strategy, channel optimization, bootstrapped marketing |
| [**Solo Founder**](agents/personas/solo-founder.md) | Cross-domain | One-person startups, side projects, MVP building, wearing all hats |

**Usage:**
```bash
# Claude Code
cp agents/personas/startup-cto.md ~/.claude/agents/

# Any tool
./scripts/convert.sh --tool cursor  # Converts personas too
```

See [agents/personas/](agents/personas/) for details. Create your own with [TEMPLATE.md](agents/personas/TEMPLATE.md).

---

## Orchestration

A lightweight protocol for coordinating personas, skills, and agents on work that crosses domain boundaries. No framework required.

**Four patterns:**

| Pattern | What | When |
|---------|------|------|
| **Solo Sprint** | Switch personas across project phases | Side projects, MVPs, solo founders |
| **Domain Deep-Dive** | One persona + multiple stacked skills | Architecture reviews, compliance audits |
| **Multi-Agent Handoff** | Personas review each other's output | High-stakes decisions, launch readiness |
| **Skill Chain** | Sequential skills, no persona needed | Content pipelines, repeatable checklists |

**Example: 6-week product launch**
```
Week 1-2: startup-cto + aws-solution-architect + senior-frontend → Build
Week 3-4: growth-marketer + launch-strategy + copywriting + seo-audit → Prepare
Week 5-6: solo-founder + email-sequence + analytics-tracking → Ship and iterate
```

## FAQ

**How do I install Claude Code plugins?**
Add the marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add alirezarezvani/claude-skills`, then install any skill bundle with `/plugin install <name>@claude-code-skills`.

**Do these skills work with OpenAI Codex / Cursor / Windsurf / Aider / Mistral Vibe?**
Yes. Skills work natively with 13 tools: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Mistral Vibe, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Augment, and Antigravity. Hermes Agent and Mistral Vibe both use the same agentskills.io SKILL.md standard — run `python scripts/sync-hermes-skills.py` or `./scripts/vibe-install.sh` to install. For other tools run `./scripts/convert.sh --tool all` then `./scripts/install.sh --tool <name>`. See [Multi-Tool Integrations](https://alirezarezvani.github.io/claude-skills/integrations/) for details.

**Will updating break my installation?**
No. We follow semantic versioning and maintain backward compatibility within patch releases. Existing script arguments, plugin source paths, and SKILL.md structures are never changed in patch versions. See the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) for details on each release.

**Are the Python tools dependency-free?**
Yes. All 824 Python tools use the standard library only — zero pip installs required. Every skill's CLI entry point is verified to run with `--help` (most skills ship one script per tool; a few, like the vendored `engineering/skillopt-sleep` engine, ship a multi-module package behind a single `python -m` entry point). A few tools — `engineering/book-to-skill`'s document extractors — can *optionally* use third-party parsers for higher-fidelity output, but every format falls back to a standard-library parser and nothing is installed implicitly.

**How do I create my own Claude Code skill?**
Each skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` (frontmatter + instructions), optional `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/`. See the [Skills & Agents Factory](https://github.com/alirezarezvani/claude-code-skills-agents-factory) for a step-by-step guide.
